label: r1c3
name: mirror flip + global context
hypothesis: Mirror flip plus the recipe with more updates, and two additions: a third residual conv with dilation 2, and a global context vector (mean and max of the features) broadcast to every cell. Placement order depends on non-local facts, such as whether supports elsewhere are already built and how much of the target is still missing. This costs about 1.3× the starting compute. Refuted if it scores below the mirror-flip run with the same recipe.
last_analysis: Flipping the features left-right is the change that matters: without it the agent always learns to stop at DONE, and with it dev success goes from 0 to 0.64–0.89. The best result is r1c3 (flip plus global context, 0.886), and both its seeds score well. None of the later changes beat it. Gamma 0.99 scored 0.846, which is within noise. Self-attention scored 0.78 and cut the sample budget. The per-layer encoder scored 0.42. The slim network with more samples scored 0.870, which ties r1c3, so width barely matters. Two results point at entropy and seed stability. Lowering ent_coef to 0.003 made both seeds worse (0.74), which suggests more exploration might help. Halving n_envs led to a full collapse to DONE on one seed. Dev IoU is about 0.98 and roughly 0.3–0.5 cells per episode land outside the target, so the remaining errors are a few wrong placements per design. For this last round I make three single changes to r1c3: a higher entropy bonus, fewer PPO epochs to get more samples, and a uniform starting policy.
